title: Hosted re-Start of a claude job past its lease TTL boots a rival worker
body:
On a deployment that binds WORKER_AGENTS, startNamedAttemptUnchecked sends a boot without claude_sub to startHostedAttempt whenever the agent's state is absent. A claude-sub container job never has an agent, so its state is always absent. Once the job outlives LEASE_TTL_MS (2h), the sticky lease has lapsed. A re-Start of the same attempt (orchestrator restart or adoption) that finds every subscription busy then steps down and starts a hosted worker on the same container name beside the running claude worker. It also overwrites the boot record's harness with pi-durable, which moves the state route and the reclaim to the agent. Separately, a lapsed lease lets the pool exceed its per-subscription cap while the job still runs. Fix: before routing, consult the recorded boot (deps.boots); an unsettled boot whose harness is not the hosted kind goes to startContainerAttempt and adopts. Also consider renewing the lease while its job is running.
evidence: cloudflare/src/sandbox-executor.ts:725-766 (routing keyed on boot.claude_sub and agent state only); cloudflare/src/claude-sub.ts:107 LEASE_TTL_MS and :331 sticky lease bounded by the TTL
